hook: What if every coding agent I run lived in _one room,_ and _called me_ when it got stuck?

problem.say: A session per project meant a dozen terminals, and _no way to see which one was waiting on me._
points: Every project ran its own Claude session in its own terminal tab, **on one Mac mini at home**.
Away from the desk, a session that stopped to ask a question **sat there for hours**.
Family members wanted to use the same agents, **without touching my terminal**.

approach.say: Keep the sessions on the Mac, and make the browser _a window onto them_, not a copy.

calls.title: One server owns every session.
calls.body: The browser can close and come back; the agent never notices.
calls.gaveUp: running agents on the phone itself.

calls.title: One folder per project, enforced.
calls.body: An agent can read the machine but write only inside its own project.
calls.gaveUp: agents that fix things across projects.

calls.title: The tailnet is the login.
calls.body: No passwords to manage; a guest gets a shared session with narrower rights.

architecture.say: The page is only a window. A server at home owns every session, _so nothing stops when you close the tab._

nodes.note: Wakes the phone when an agent waits

steps.text: The message leaves the phone over HTTPS; Tailscale says who sent it.
The server checks that this person may use this project, and saves the message.
It hands the message to the project's agent, which keeps working if you close the page.
The agent thinks with the Claude API and edits only its own folder.
The agent asks for permission; the server marks the session as needing you.
A push wakes the phone, even with the page closed.
One tap answers it, and the agent carries on where it stopped.

results.say: It replaced the terminal for _everyday work._
